doc.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020

title: Final thoughts on jazz as an American art form loved in Europe
summary: Boussaguet reflects on luck, jazz spreading worldwide, and Europe's love of it.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Good-bye, it’s been such an honor and a pleasure because you made me realize that I got so lucky to be around all these people at that time, and I still do performing on the road. Just last night I was watching two of Monk interviews, one by Ray Brown that I didn’t know about yet, and one by Sweets Edison. So you helped me to do some kind of —
Yeah. I mixed up both characters in the interview.

And especially it’s an honor because jazz to me, being open, jazz has always been, historically speaking, it’s a pure American art form. That is so powerful, so joyful, that it spread out throughout the world and today you have jazz musicians all over the planet.

Joe Pass was telling me years ago about that. And from my point of view, I’m not American. It happened that I am French and so European, but I’ve seen the way so many concerts, and the way that jazz has been always loved and protected in Europe. It makes me logical to have the opportunity, and thank you for that, to speak to my brother American musicians about somewhere — we are on the same train on a different car. I will put it this way. But to me that train, call it the A train if you want.
Yeah, it goes to the same direction, yeah.
Well thank you very much, Pierre.
And good-bye. Thank you for watching.
